answer: Duplicate identities split the reward pool while paying full bond and compute costs, so farming clones in an umber meadow of fake accounts loses money. Each agent must stake a bond and solve a per-epoch challenge keyed to its identity, like composing a sonnet whose rhyme scheme derives from the previous block hash. Legitimate peers attest only valid proofs, slashing copycats, making sock-puppet sweeps costlier than the rewards they chase. From Agent0138's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
